subject: science
passage: Polar bears look white, but their fur is not actually white at all. Each outer hair is ______, containing no pigment, and is hollow at its core. The hairs appear white for the same reason snow does: they scatter all colors of visible light. Beneath this coat, a polar bear's skin is black.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The text says the fur is "not actually white" and that each hair contains "no pigment," the substance that gives things color. A hair without any color of its own is colorless, so "colorless" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. A hair with "no pigment" has no color of its own; it only looks white because it scatters light, so it is colorless.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A hair "containing no pigment" cannot be dark. It is the bear's skin, not its hair, that is black.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text mentions stripes; it says the hairs have no color at all.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text does not discuss how thick the hairs are; the phrase "containing no pigment" shows the blank is about color.
